data.title: fix(dagre): merge flowchart and state self-loop segments before rendering
data.body: ## :bookmark_tabs: Summary Fixes flowchart and stateDiagram-v2 self-loop edges so that one logical self-loop is rendered as one SVG `` instead of three internal dagre layout segments. Resolves #6336 ### Background I first noticed this while frequently editing Mermaid flowcharts through the GUI at https://mermaid.ai/. That editor is not part of this open-source repository, but it made the issue very visible: self-loop edges could not be edited reliably through the GUI. Deleting the edge, selecting it, or editing its text did not work the same way as regular edges. After inspecting the generated SVG, I found that a single logical self-loop such as: ```mermaid flowchart TD C --> C ``` was not represented as a single SVG edge path. Instead, it was rendered as multiple `` elements with internal ids similar to: ```html ``` This made downstream SVG-based tooling treat one logical edge as several visual edges. The same multi-path self-loop behavior was also visible when testing in Mermaid's own rendering output, so the root issue appeared to be in Mermaid core rendering rather than only in external GUI tooling. This PR changes the final SVG output for flowcharts and stateDiagram-v2 diagrams so that a logical self-loop edge maps back to a single rendered path. ### Before / After Before: clicking a self-loop edge selects one of three split SVG path segments instead of a single logical edge, so GUI operations such as editing the label or deleting the edge do not work reliably. After: the same self-loop now appears as one compact SVG path for the logical edge, preventing the GUI from treating its internal layout segments as separate editable edges. ## :straight_ruler: Design Decisions ### Root Cause The issue comes from the dagre layout adapter: ```text packages/mermaid/src/rendering-util/layout-algorithms/dagre/index.js ``` For self-loops, the adapter intentionally creates dummy nodes and splits one logical edge into three internal layout edges: ```text node -> dummy node 1 -> dummy node 2 -> node ``` That workaround is useful for layout because it gives dagre a route that can produce a loop-like shape. The problem was that these internal layout segments were still passed directly to the SVG edge renderer after layout. Since the renderer draws one `` per edge object, one logical self-loop became three public SVG paths. ### Chosen Fix This PR keeps the existing dagre dummy-node workaround for layout stability, but converts flowchart and stateDiagram-v2 self-loop segments back into one render edge before SVG insertion. The new flow is: ```text Input: C --> C Dagre layout graph: C -> dummy1 -> dummy2 -> C Render preparation: group the three self-loop segments by the original edge id compute one compact self-loop route around the node create one merged render edge Final SVG: one logical self-loop = one ``` This avoids relying on dagre to natively produce good self-loop geometry for every rank direction, node shape, label size, and cluster case. At the same time, it prevents internal layout implementation details from leaking into the final SVG DOM. ### Why Not Remove the Dummy Edges Entirely? The simplest-looking change would be to stop splitting self-loops and call dagre with a direct self-edge: ```js graph.setEdge(nodeId, nodeId, edge, edge.id); ``` I did not choose that approach because the existing dummy-node logic appears to be there to stabilize self-loop layout. Removing it would change the layout input more dramatically and could introduce regressions in complex diagrams. Instead, this PR makes a smaller change: - keep the layout workaround - preserve the original edge metadata on the three internal segments - merge those segments immediately before rendering - render one path for the logical self-loop - leave class diagrams on the existing segmented rendering path because self-referential multiplicity labels rely on that behavior ### Compact Self-loop Shape Simply concatenating dagre's three segment point lists can still produce very large or awkward self-loops. This PR computes a compact loop around the original node for the final render edge. The generated loop uses: - the original node position - the original node width and height - the self-loop label size - the graph direction - dagre's dummy node positions as layout hints This keeps the self-loop visually small and close to the node, instead of producing a long route that looks like several unrelated edge segments. ### Side Selection The self-loop is not always forced to the top of the node. The implementation first looks at where dagre placed the dummy nodes and uses that as a hint for which side of the node the loop should attach to. If those hints are unavailable, it falls back to the graph direction: ```text TB -> top BT -> bottom LR -> right RL -> left ``` This keeps the loop placement closer to dagre's layout result while still producing deterministic output. ### Label Handling Before layout, edge labels are inserted while the three self-loop layout segments already exist. To avoid duplicate labels, only the middle segment inserts the label. During that label insertion, the segment temporarily uses the original edge id so that the label is associated with the final merged render edge. This merged-path behavior is scoped to `flowchart`, `flowchart-v2`, and `stateDiagram`. Other dagre-based diagrams, including class diagrams, keep the previous segmented self-loop rendering behavior. ### Fallback Behavior If a self-loop group does not contain exactly three expected segments, the implementation falls back to rendering the original segments rather than dropping the edge. This is intentional. In unexpected graph states, preserving the previous visible output is safer than making the edge disappear. ### Files Changed ```text packages/mermaid/src/rendering-util/layout-algorithms/dagre/index.js packages/mermaid/src/rendering-util/layout-algorithms/dagre/index.spec.js cypress/integration/rendering/flowchart/flowchart-v2.spec.js cypress/integration/rendering/state/stateDiagram-v2.spec.js ``` ### Tests Added Added targeted tests for the dagre self-loop rendering flow: - verifies that three internal self-loop layout segments become one render edge - verifies that self-loop side placement can follow dagre layout hints - verifies that regular edges pass through unchanged - renders a real Mermaid flowchart in JSDOM and checks that the self-loop appears as one SVG path - verifies that internal `cyclic-special` path ids are not exposed as rendered self-loop paths - verifies that the generated self-loop route stays compact - adds Cypress visual coverage for labeled flowchart self-loops - adds Cypress visual coverage for non-TB flowchart self-loop directions - adds Cypress visual coverage for the #6336 `stateDiagram-v2` self-loop reproduction Targeted command run: ```sh pnpm exec vitest run packages/mermaid/src/rendering-util/layout-algorithms/dagre/index.spec.js ``` Result: ```text 1 test file passed 5 tests passed ``` The test run also emitted existing Vite/TypeScript `TS5055: Cannot write file ... because it would overwrite input file` warnings, but those warnings did not fail the targeted test suite. ### Expected Impact After this change: - a logical self-loop edge renders as one SVG path - self-loop internals such as `cyclic-special-1`, `cyclic-special-mid`, and `cyclic-special-2` are no longer exposed as separate rendered paths - SVG-based tools can map a self-loop path back to a single logical edge more reliably - self-loop geometry is more compact and visually attached to the node - regular edges keep their existing rendering behavior - stateDiagram-v2 self-loops use the same compact single-path rendering - class diagrams keep their existing segmented self-loop behavior This should also help SVG-based GUI editors, including Mermaid AI, map flowchart self-loops back to a single editable edge for selection, deletion, and label editing. ### :clipboard: Tasks Make sure you - [x] :book: have read the [contribution guidelines](https://mermaid.js.org/community/contributing.html) - [x] :computer: have added necessary unit/e2e tests. - [x] :notebook: have added documentation. Make sure [`MERMAID_RELEASE_VERSION`](https://mermaid.js.org/community/contributing.html#update-documentation) is used for all new features. - [x] :butterfly: If your PR makes a change that should be noted in one or more packages' changelogs, generate a changeset by running `pnpm changeset` and following the prompts. Changesets that add features should be `minor` and those that fix bugs should be `patch`. Please prefix changeset messages with `feat:`, `fix:`, or `chore:`.

Updated the patch to scope self-loop segment merging to flowcharts only.

The failing E2E case was a class diagram self-reference with multiplicity labels. Class diagrams also use the dagre self-loop segment workaround, but they rely on the existing segmented rendering for terminal label placement. To avoid changing non-flowchart behavior, self-loop merging is now enabled only for `flowchart` / `flowchart-v2`, and I added a unit test to ensure segments are preserved when merging is disabled.

@ashishjain0512 Thanks a lot for the very detailed review. The feedback was extremely helpful, especially the points about the linked issue scope and the additional visual coverage needed to lock in the new geometry. I took the first path you suggested and expanded the self-loop segment merge gate to include stateDiagram in addition to flowchart / flowchart-v2. stateDiagram-v2 is registered through stateDetector-V2.ts with the diagram type stateDiagram, so the #6336 reproduction: now goes through the same self-loop segment merging path. Because of that, I think keeping Resolves #6336 is now accurate. I intentionally left class diagrams on the existing segmented rendering path. The earlier E2E failure for a self-referential class diagram with multiplicity labels showed that class diagrams rely on the existing segmented self-loop behavior for terminal label placement. I wanted to avoid broadening the behavior there without a more diagram-specific follow-up. I also added Cypress visual coverage for the cases you called out: labeled flowchart self-loops non-TB flowchart self-loop directions the #6336 stateDiagram-v2 self-loop reproduction I also cleaned up the small unit-test nit around setOnProtectedConstant. The targeted dagre unit tests pass locally: pnpm exec vitest run packages/mermaid/src/rendering-util/layout-algorithms/dagre/index.spec.js Result: 5 tests passed I also attempted to run the full pnpm e2e suite locally, but my local Windows harness did not complete cleanly due to environment/process startup issues before Cypress results were produced. I am relying on the PR CI E2E matrix for the full browser coverage. For Argos: the expected visual changes are the flowchart/stateDiagram self-loop snapshots, since this PR intentionally changes self-loop geometry. I also noticed a few unrelated-looking diffs, such as quadrant-chart screenshots. I checked the rendering path, and quadrant charts use their own quadrantRenderer.ts rather than the dagre layout adapter changed in this PR, so those do not appear to be caused by the self-loop merge logic. Thanks again for the careful review. Your comments helped make the PR scope and test coverage much clearer.

Testing the rendered shape's bounding box or point count would be more stable.

I came here to post about this issue as well. It gets wild if you're trying to illustrate a finite state machine:
```
stateDiagram-v2
  A --> B
  B-->B
  B -->A
  A --> C
  C --> C
  C --> B
  C --> A
```

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dc42f1c7-6763-4371-934b-25fd7c20227d)

Hello,

I completely agree that self-loops in **Mermaid state diagrams** currently do not render as cleanly as they do in **Graphviz digraphs**. The issue appears to stem from how self-loops are treated like standard edges rather than being explicitly optimized for circular positioning.

### Possible Issues in the Current Implementation
**1. Lack of Explicit Self-Loop Handling**
- The `stateDb.js` processing functions that do not differentiate self-loops from regular transitions.
- As a result, the self-loop is drawn as a reversed transition rather than a properly curved arc.

**2. Edge Routing & Layout Constraints**
- The automatic layout engine does not prioritize self-loops, causing them to be positioned awkwardly.
- Graphviz, by contrast, uses **explicit loop placement** rules that result in smoother loops.

**3. Styling & Customization Limitations**
- The `setStyle()` function in `stateDb.js` does not provide options for defining self-loop curvature or positioning.
- Unlike Graphviz, Mermaid does not support **loop-specific attributes** like `headport` or `tailport` to adjust where the loop attaches to the node.

### Possible Fixes & Enhancements
- Introduce **explicit self-loop detection**, ensuring that self-loops are styled separately from regular edges.
- Add support for **loop curvature controls** in `setStyle()`, similar to how Graphviz allows adjustments.
- Implement **edge anchor customization** (e.g., allowing users to specify where the self-loop attaches to the node).

Would love to hear your thoughts.

Hello @hjfreyer 

I have also tested self-loops across multiple diagram types and confirm that the issue affects state diagrams class diagrams and flowcharts, where loops are misaligned, overlapping, or bending unnaturally even when forcing a horizontal layout. 

However, like you mentioned for graphviz,  sequence diagrams also render self-loops correctly, which requires further investigation.



Screenshots for Reference:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0e426bfe-096a-4dd1-837b-3f2da3e7bd56)


![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e96a6119-454f-4b94-b649-7e493934fa45)

- Correct self-loops in sequence diagrams
- Misaligned self-loops in state diagrams and flowcharts
Can we expect an ETA on this?
FWIW, this is appears to be a regression from 10.x.

``` stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> s1 s1 --> [*] s1 --> s2 s2 --> s3 s2 --> s2 s3 --> s4 s3 --> s3 s4 --> s5 s4 --> s4 s5 --> s1 s5 --> s5 ```

creates this graph in v11:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/045b0c15-8059-417b-af68-fc0acc481ac1)

and created this graph in v10:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bbb96059-9f77-40e1-be78-04b44e082c17)

Unfortunately, it seems to get worse when adding multiplicities:


![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bb71c7dc-6ec9-4c1f-b127-0260adf060d7)

There is way to many "1"s and "n"s there...

Having the same problem in Visual Studio Code with Mermaid extension (v2.4.1). For flowcharts, one can change the rendering engine in the configuration to `"elk"` as a workaround: ### Without config change: ```mmd flowchart LR A --->|foo| B B --->|bar| B ``` ### With config change: ```mmd %%{ init: { 'flowchart': {'defaultRenderer': 'elk' } } }%% flowchart LR A --->|foo| B B --->|bar| B ``` See in [live editor](https://mermaid.live/edit#pako:eNpdkTFvgzAQhf-KdRJiIREpxhgPlZp2bJd0q7y4cBBUsCPXbpsS_nsdSDL0bnqf7u496UaoTI0gIIpG0unOCTKSuOnNd7VX1sVBxjU2yvduh7pGizawGPuPmEznjiKpb-PkeSc1CfVAVqvV_akx5kS2C9ou6F3ZGUECre1qEM56TGBAO6izhFGC2-OAEgSRcPGWkARReft14X2nUdkF_8u3DISEEqbgclD6zZjhamSNb_cgGtV_BuUPtXL41KnWquFG7Xzp0XjtQLAsm4-AGOEHBC_X_I5yxnjJWJHyIoEjiE2erTllZcZplpe0ZPmUwO9sm65zyguWZ-mmSClNWdhQ3pnXo66uobDunLEvyyfmh0x_Yex-Tg).

[sisyphus-bot]

Thanks for the detailed report and comparison with Graphviz, @hjfreyer.

We've flagged this for maintainer review because self-loop edge rendering likely involves **shared edge routing code** in `rendering-util/` that all diagram types use.

**Initial analysis:**
- Self-loops in state diagrams are rendered using the general edge routing system
- The current routing doesn't have special-case handling for self-edges — they use the same path calculation as regular edges, producing the awkward "kink" shape
- Improving self-loops would require changes to edge routing in `rendering-util/`, which affects all diagram types (flowchart, class, state, etc.)
- The Graphviz approach (side-mounted circular loop) is the standard UML convention and would be a significant rendering improvement

Multiple users have confirmed this is a pain point. A maintainer will evaluate the self-loop rendering approach. Thanks!

issue.body: ## :bookmark_tabs: Summary Fixes flowchart and stateDiagram-v2 self-loop edges so that one logical self-loop is rendered as one SVG `` instead of three internal dagre layout segments. Resolves #6336 ### Background I first noticed this while frequently editing Mermaid flowcharts through the GUI at https://mermaid.ai/. That editor is not part of this open-source repository, but it made the issue very visible: self-loop edges could not be edited reliably through the GUI. Deleting the edge, selecting it, or editing its text did not work the same way as regular edges. After inspecting the generated SVG, I found that a single logical self-loop such as: ```mermaid flowchart TD C --> C ``` was not represented as a single SVG edge path. Instead, it was rendered as multiple `` elements with internal ids similar to: ```html ``` This made downstream SVG-based tooling treat one logical edge as several visual edges. The same multi-path self-loop behavior was also visible when testing in Mermaid's own rendering output, so the root issue appeared to be in Mermaid core rendering rather than only in external GUI tooling. This PR changes the final SVG output for flowcharts and stateDiagram-v2 diagrams so that a logical self-loop edge maps back to a single rendered path. ### Before / After Before: clicking a self-loop edge selects one of three split SVG path segments instead of a single logical edge, so GUI operations such as editing the label or deleting the edge do not work reliably. After: the same self-loop now appears as one compact SVG path for the logical edge, preventing the GUI from treating its internal layout segments as separate editable edges. ## :straight_ruler: Design Decisions ### Root Cause The issue comes from the dagre layout adapter: ```text packages/mermaid/src/rendering-util/layout-algorithms/dagre/index.js ``` For self-loops, the adapter intentionally creates dummy nodes and splits one logical edge into three internal layout edges: ```text node -> dummy node 1 -> dummy node 2 -> node ``` That workaround is useful for layout because it gives dagre a route that can produce a loop-like shape. The problem was that these internal layout segments were still passed directly to the SVG edge renderer after layout. Since the renderer draws one `` per edge object, one logical self-loop became three public SVG paths. ### Chosen Fix This PR keeps the existing dagre dummy-node workaround for layout stability, but converts flowchart and stateDiagram-v2 self-loop segments back into one render edge before SVG insertion. The new flow is: ```text Input: C --> C Dagre layout graph: C -> dummy1 -> dummy2 -> C Render preparation: group the three self-loop segments by the original edge id compute one compact self-loop route around the node create one merged render edge Final SVG: one logical self-loop = one ``` This avoids relying on dagre to natively produce good self-loop geometry for every rank direction, node shape, label size, and cluster case. At the same time, it prevents internal layout implementation details from leaking into the final SVG DOM. ### Why Not Remove the Dummy Edges Entirely? The simplest-looking change would be to stop splitting self-loops and call dagre with a direct self-edge: ```js graph.setEdge(nodeId, nodeId, edge, edge.id); ``` I did not choose that approach because the existing dummy-node logic appears to be there to stabilize self-loop layout. Removing it would change the layout input more dramatically and could introduce regressions in complex diagrams. Instead, this PR makes a smaller change: - keep the layout workaround - preserve the original edge metadata on the three internal segments - merge those segments immediately before rendering - render one path for the logical self-loop - leave class diagrams on the existing segmented rendering path because self-referential multiplicity labels rely on that behavior ### Compact Self-loop Shape Simply concatenating dagre's three segment point lists can still produce very large or awkward self-loops. This PR computes a compact loop around the original node for the final render edge. The generated loop uses: - the original node position - the original node width and height - the self-loop label size - the graph direction - dagre's dummy node positions as layout hints This keeps the self-loop visually small and close to the node, instead of producing a long route that looks like several unrelated edge segments. ### Side Selection The self-loop is not always forced to the top of the node. The implementation first looks at where dagre placed the dummy nodes and uses that as a hint for which side of the node the loop should attach to. If those hints are unavailable, it falls back to the graph direction: ```text TB -> top BT -> bottom LR -> right RL -> left ``` This keeps the loop placement closer to dagre's layout result while still producing deterministic output. ### Label Handling Before layout, edge labels are inserted while the three self-loop layout segments already exist. To avoid duplicate labels, only the middle segment inserts the label. During that label insertion, the segment temporarily uses the original edge id so that the label is associated with the final merged render edge. This merged-path behavior is scoped to `flowchart`, `flowchart-v2`, and `stateDiagram`. Other dagre-based diagrams, including class diagrams, keep the previous segmented self-loop rendering behavior. ### Fallback Behavior If a self-loop group does not contain exactly three expected segments, the implementation falls back to rendering the original segments rather than dropping the edge. This is intentional. In unexpected graph states, preserving the previous visible output is safer than making the edge disappear. ### Files Changed ```text packages/mermaid/src/rendering-util/layout-algorithms/dagre/index.js packages/mermaid/src/rendering-util/layout-algorithms/dagre/index.spec.js cypress/integration/rendering/flowchart/flowchart-v2.spec.js cypress/integration/rendering/state/stateDiagram-v2.spec.js ``` ### Tests Added Added targeted tests for the dagre self-loop rendering flow: - verifies that three internal self-loop layout segments become one render edge - verifies that self-loop side placement can follow dagre layout hints - verifies that regular edges pass through unchanged - renders a real Mermaid flowchart in JSDOM and checks that the self-loop appears as one SVG path - verifies that internal `cyclic-special` path ids are not exposed as rendered self-loop paths - verifies that the generated self-loop route stays compact - adds Cypress visual coverage for labeled flowchart self-loops - adds Cypress visual coverage for non-TB flowchart self-loop directions - adds Cypress visual coverage for the #6336 `stateDiagram-v2` self-loop reproduction Targeted command run: ```sh pnpm exec vitest run packages/mermaid/src/rendering-util/layout-algorithms/dagre/index.spec.js ``` Result: ```text 1 test file passed 5 tests passed ``` The test run also emitted existing Vite/TypeScript `TS5055: Cannot write file ... because it would overwrite input file` warnings, but those warnings did not fail the targeted test suite. ### Expected Impact After this change: - a logical self-loop edge renders as one SVG path - self-loop internals such as `cyclic-special-1`, `cyclic-special-mid`, and `cyclic-special-2` are no longer exposed as separate rendered paths - SVG-based tools can map a self-loop path back to a single logical edge more reliably - self-loop geometry is more compact and visually attached to the node - regular edges keep their existing rendering behavior - stateDiagram-v2 self-loops use the same compact single-path rendering - class diagrams keep their existing segmented self-loop behavior This should also help SVG-based GUI editors, including Mermaid AI, map flowchart self-loops back to a single editable edge for selection, deletion, and label editing. ### :clipboard: Tasks Make sure you - Research from GPT 5.5 Pro
# Agentic Mermaid: Relevant Renderer Gaps and Port/Anchor Policy

_Use this as a GitHub-issue seed for `adewale/beautiful-mermaid` / Agentic Mermaid._

Last reviewed: 2026-06-14.

## Thesis

Agentic Mermaid should absorb the useful lessons from Mermaid.js, upstream Beautiful Mermaid, and Mermaid ASCII by turning renderer-specific guesswork into explicit, testable contracts.

The goal is **not** visual parity with Mermaid.js. The goal is deterministic, source-preserving, agent-verifiable rendering and editing across SVG, PNG, ASCII/Unicode, and layout JSON.

In scope:

- no silent syntax loss
- route classes before layout
- semantic ports and shape-aware anchors
- proof-carrying route repairs
- Mermaid link length honored in placement
- SVG/ASCII/Unicode route-intent parity
- source span / semantic object / rendered region traceability
- family-specific layout validators
- deterministic quality and golden evidence
- structured warnings when unsupported syntax or degraded rendering occurs

Out of scope:

- changing Mermaid.js public syntax
- matching Mermaid.js pixel layout
- copying upstream Beautiful Mermaid hacks wholesale
- supporting every Mermaid family without evidence
- generic typography, accessibility, or security rewrites unless they affect source preservation, layout correctness, or agent verification

## Why this is fork-relevant

Agentic Mermaid is not just a renderer. The repository positions it as a Mermaid rendering and editing toolkit for deterministic ASCII, PNG, SVG, JSON layout, and agent-verifiable structured edits. The README also documents a parse → narrow → mutate → verify → serialize workflow for supported structured diagram families. That makes weak parsing, silent loss, and renderer-only layout heuristics more dangerous here than they are in a display-only tool.

The current fork already has issues and PRs pointing in the right direction:

- Issue #26 argues for replacing renderer-specific hacks with principled contracts across parsing, semantic modeling, layout intent, certificates/diagnostics, rendering, and validation.
- Issue #26 specifically calls for semantic route classes, semantic ports, shape-aware anchors, and fixed-side ports where useful.
- PR #30 is already a route-contract effort around proof-carrying repairs, port ranking, port-lane alignment, route certificates, and endpoint correctness.
- Issue #32 tracks honoring Mermaid link rank-distance / link length in layout.
- Issue #36 tracks unsupported flowchart syntax that must be supported or surfaced loudly instead of silently dropped.

Do not duplicate those blindly. Use this document as a distilled backlog and a policy sketch for a follow-up issue.

---

# Part 1: Relevant complaints distilled from other Mermaid variants

## 1. Silent syntax loss is unacceptable

Mermaid.js can get away with fuzzy parsing because it is primarily a renderer. Agentic Mermaid cannot. An agent editing a diagram needs to know whether syntax was:

1. understood structurally,
2. preserved opaquely,
3. normalized with a warning, or
4. rejected.

There should be no silent fifth state.

Keep these cases in scope:

```text
@{ shape: ... } node metadata
edge IDs like e1@-->
edge metadata @{...}
newer shape aliases
mixed & chains
link styling shorthand
invisible links
variable-length links
unsupported flowchart syntax that currently becomes phantom nodes
unsupported flowchart syntax that verifies ok despite lost meaning
```

Rule:

> Parse it, preserve it, or warn/error. No fourth option.

## 2. Route intent must be modeled before layout

The useful complaint against Mermaid.js and upstream Beautiful Mermaid is not simply that their layouts are ugly. It is that they feed layout engines too little semantic intent, then patch the output afterward.

Agentic Mermaid should classify graph-like edges before layout:

```text
primary-forward
feedback
fanout
fanin
sibling-branch
self-loop
cross-hierarchy
container-edge
relation
dependency
exception
```

This matters because SVG, PNG, ASCII/Unicode, and layout JSON must agree. If every renderer guesses edge semantics independently, parity will rot.

## 3. Ports and shape-aware anchors are fork-relevant as an internal contract

Do not phrase this as “Mermaid.js should add port syntax.” That is upstream-language design.

The fork-relevant version is:

> Agentic Mermaid should infer, store, certify, and expose semantic ports/anchors even when Mermaid source lacks explicit port syntax.

The port model should cover:

```text
canonical side for primary-forward edges
alternative side for feedback edges
ordered ports for fanout/fanin
diamond vertex/midpoint anchors
circle/stadium/parallelogram/trapezoid endpoint oracles
subgraph/container boundary ports
self-loop anchor policy
SVG/ASCII/Unicode/layout-json agreement on chosen ports
```

## 4. Proof-carrying repairs are relevant; blind beautification is not

A renderer can straighten hitches, snap layers, clip shapes, and bundle edges. Those passes become dangerous if they mutate geometry without proving what changed.

Policy:

```text
No cleanup pass may mutate final geometry unless it emits a certificate
or invalidates/recomputes existing certificates.
```

Useful diagnostics:

```text
ROUTE_HITCH
EDGE_MISANCHORED
EDGE_OFF_PORT
PORT_ORDER_VIOLATED
PORT_CONSTRAINT_RELAXED
UNEXPLAINED_DETOUR
LABEL_ON_WRONG_BRANCH
GROUP_BREACH
EDGE_NODE_COLLISION
ROUTE_SELF_CROSS
```

## 5. Mermaid link length must affect layout, not just parsing

Mermaid link length is layout intent. `A --> B` and `A ----> B` should not necessarily place the target in the same rank distance. If the parser captures link length but layout ignores it, Agentic Mermaid is preserving syntax while losing semantics.

Acceptance criteria:

```text
all four directions tested: LR, RL, TD, BT
lengthened edge increases rank distance
base-length output unchanged
route contracts still apply after dummy rank insertion or equivalent layer handling
no new hitches, occlusions, or bogus route certificates
```

## 6. ASCII/Unicode must consume the same semantic layout intent as SVG

ASCII renderers often become separate approximations: their own pathfinder, labels, subgraph behavior, and bugs. That is wrong for Agentic Mermaid.

ASCII/Unicode should project the same route classes, ports, labels, container edges, and certificates used by SVG.

Keep this scope:

```text
same route class as SVG
same branch label ownership
same container-edge semantics
deterministic pathfinder tie-breaking
exact ASCII/Unicode goldens
cell-level metadata tied to semantic object IDs
warning when ASCII cannot preserve a semantic distinction
```

Do not make this a general terminal-rendering crusade. Width policy, ANSI coloring, CJK, emoji, and wrapping matter only when they cause source loss, bad geometry, unverifiable regions, or label/route collisions.

## 7. Source preservation and wrapper fidelity matter because agents edit source

A renderer-only architecture treats source as an input string. Agentic Mermaid treats source as an editable artifact. That requires knowing which source spans are safe to mutate.

Relevant work:

```text
byte-verbatim frontmatter/directive/comment preservation
source span → semantic object → rendered region mapping
structured-or-opaque fallback per family
segment-preserving bodies, not whole-diagram opaque fallback
mutation ops that refuse unsafe edits instead of regenerating the whole source
```

## 8. Family-specific contracts matter more than generic graph layout

Do not push every diagram family through generic graph heuristics. Each family needs its own semantic layout contract and validators.

Keep these family-specific slices:

```text
Flowchart/state:
- route classes
- ports
- branch labels
- feedback loops
- subgraph/container boundaries

Class:
- class box compartments
- relation labels
- dependency/relation endpoints
- no silent member truncation

ER:
- cardinality markers are endpoint-owned semantic glyphs
- relation labels reserve endpoint/corridor space
- malformed relationship lines error loudly

Architecture:
- service/group/junction edge semantics
- side-anchored edges
- group/container crossing behavior

Sequence:
- participant/lifeline/message region stability
- segment-preserving opaque blocks

Charts/timeline/journey/pie/quadrant:
- not graph edges unless they really are
- quality metrics should use marks/regions, not pretend everything is nodes and edges
```

## 9. Quality metrics and evidence gates are relevant; “looks nicer” is not

Translate “ugly layout” into measurable gates.

Every visual/layout fix should have:

```text
red-first fixture
before/after render evidence
geometry assertions
route/layout certificates where applicable
SVG and ASCII/Unicode parity checks where applicable
no unexplained metric regression
```

Drop vague goals like:

```text
Make it look more like Mermaid.
```

The better goal is:

```text
Make it faithful, deterministic, source-preserving, and agent-verifiable.
```

## 10. Text measurement matters only where it affects correctness

Text measurement is fork-relevant when it affects:

```text
label overflow detection
node sizing
route-label collision checks
ASCII column width
CJK/fullwidth/emoji warnings when deterministic sizing is uncertain
shared measurement between layout and quality metrics
```

Do not turn this into a full typography engine unless it blocks correctness.

## 11. Security/action records are relevant if interactivity is preserved

If Agentic Mermaid parses interactive/action syntax, strict security behavior should be centralized and renderer-independent.

Policy:

```text
Parse action-like syntax into inert action records with a security disposition.
SVG, PNG, ASCII, and layout JSON should agree on the semantic record,
even if only SVG can expose an actual link.
```

Lower priority unless agent workflows edit or preserve `click`, `href`, or tooltip syntax.

## 12. Compatibility with Mermaid’s family catalogue should be evidence-driven

Do not chase Mermaid’s full diagram catalogue just to match a table.

Keep:

```text
evidence-driven family additions
source-level first implementation is acceptable
structured mutation only when semantics can be preserved
explicit unsupported syntax
no invented Mermaid syntax
```

Drop:

```text
Support all Mermaid families now.
Match Mermaid’s renderer for everything.
```

---

# Part 2: Items to avoid in this issue

Drop these from a fork issue unless they are promoted into focused work with fixtures:

```text
Mermaid.js should change its public flowchart syntax.
Mermaid.js should default to ELK.
Mermaid.js should expose ports.
Mermaid.js should become deterministic.
Mermaid.js should optimize for agents.
Beautiful Mermaid upstream should adopt the Agentic Mermaid model.
Mermaid ASCII should become a full semantic renderer by itself.
Agentic Mermaid should chase pixel parity with Mermaid.
Agentic Mermaid should support every Mermaid family before preserving source correctly.
Agentic Mermaid should port old Dagre-specific layout hacks.
Agentic Mermaid should absorb Vercel/package/branding choices from other forks.
```

---

# Part 3: Port system policy

## Short answer

A diamond should have **four canonical anchor sites**, not “four total ports.”

A decision diamond usually has at least **three semantic roles**:

```text
primary input
true/yes/primary output
false/no/alternate output
```

But the number of actual port instances is dynamic. It depends on the incident edges, route classes, labels, fanout/fanin grouping, self-loops, and container crossings.

So the correct model is:

```text
shape defines canonical anchor sites
semantics choose sides/roles
incident edges instantiate ordered ports
shape oracle computes exact boundary contact
route certificate records the decision
```

Do **not** define a diamond as “one center port” or “exactly four ports forever.” Both are wrong.

## Terminology

Use these terms consistently.

```ts
type PortSide = 'NORTH' | 'EAST' | 'SOUTH' | 'WEST'

type PortConstraint =
  | 'FREE'
  | 'FIXED_SIDE'
  | 'FIXED_ORDER'
  | 'FIXED_RATIO'
  | 'FIXED_POS'

type RouteClass =
  | 'primary-forward'
  | 'feedback'
  | 'fanout'
  | 'fanin'
  | 'sibling-branch'
  | 'self-loop'
  | 'cross-hierarchy'
  | 'container-edge'
  | 'relation'
  | 'dependency'
  | 'exception'
```

Suggested object split:

```ts
interface SemanticPortRole {
  id: string                 // e.g. "decision.yes", "primary.in", "feedback.out"
  direction: 'in' | 'out' | 'both'
  preferredSide: PortSide
  fallbackSides: PortSide[]
  routeClasses: RouteClass[]
}

interface PortInstance {
  id: string                 // stable, edge-endpoint-addressable
  nodeId: string
  edgeId?: string
  roleId?: string
  side: PortSide
  order?: number             // side-local order
  constraint: PortConstraint
}

interface AnchorCandidate {
  side: PortSide
  kind: 'vertex' | 'side-midpoint' | 'side-slot' | 'radial' | 'boundary-slot'
  ratio?: number             // side-relative slot if not exact vertex/midpoint
  cost: number
  reason: string
}
```

ELK already has the relevant conceptual ladder: `FREE`, `FIXED_SIDE`, `FIXED_ORDER`, `FIXED_RATIO`, and `FIXED_POS`. It also has explicit port sides `NORTH`, `EAST`, `SOUTH`, and `WEST`. Agentic Mermaid should generally start with `FIXED_SIDE` and `FIXED_ORDER`, not `FIXED_POS`, unless exact shape semantics require a specific anchor.

## The core rule

Do not ask:

> How many ports does this shape have?

Ask:

> What canonical anchor sites does this shape expose, and how many edge endpoints need ordered port instances on those sites?

Formula:

```text
canonicalAnchorSites = shape family contract
semanticRoles       = diagram family + node role + route class
portInstances       = one per edge endpoint, optionally grouped by semantic role
sideOrder           = source/model order first, crossing minimizer second
exactContactPoint   = shape oracle(anchor site, route vector, rendered geometry)
```

A shape can expose four canonical sites while a node has one, three, seven, or twenty actual port instances.

## Diamond policy

### Canonical anchor sites

A diamond should expose these four canonical sites:

```text
NORTH vertex
EAST vertex
SOUTH vertex
WEST vertex
```

These are anchor sites, not the entire port count.

### Decision-role defaults

For a top-down (`TD`) decision diamond:

```text
primary incoming: NORTH
primary/yes outgoing: SOUTH
no/else outgoing: EAST by default, WEST if that reduces crossing or follows model order
feedback: WEST/EAST, not SOUTH unless semantically forward
self-loop: side with least conflict, usually EAST or WEST
```

For a left-right (`LR`) decision diamond:

```text
primary incoming: WEST
primary/yes outgoing: EAST
no/else outgoing: SOUTH by default, NORTH if that reduces crossing or follows model order
feedback: NORTH/SOUTH, not EAST unless semantically forward
self-loop: side with least conflict, usually NORTH or SOUTH
```

For `BT` and `RL`, mirror the `TD` and `LR` rules.

### The yes/no caveat

Do not hard-code English labels only. Use labels as hints, not sole truth.

Useful branch-label hints:

```text
yes / true / success / ok / pass / valid / found / exists
no / false / failure / error / fail / invalid / missing / else
```

But route class, graph direction, source order, target rank, and cycle analysis should outrank label text.

### Number of actual diamond ports

For a normal binary decision in `TD`:

```text
incoming edge: 1 port instance on NORTH
yes edge:      1 port instance on SOUTH
no edge:       1 port instance on EAST or WEST
```

That node has three actual port instances, using three of four canonical sites.

If it has both `yes` and `no` plus a feedback edge:

```text
incoming: 1 NORTH
yes:      1 SOUTH
no:       1 EAST
feedback: 1 WEST
```

That node has four actual port instances.

If it fans out to three `yes` targets:

```text
incoming: 1 NORTH
yes:      3 ordered SOUTH-side port instances
no:       1 EAST or WEST
```

That node has five actual port instances.


### Eight diamond ports and reciprocal pairs

Adding eight physical diamond anchors is **not inherently a mistake**. It is useful for reciprocal pairs and local congestion. It becomes a mistake only if the semantic model says:

```text
diamond = exactly 8 ports
```

Use this instead:

```text
diamond = 4 canonical semantic sides/sites
side = NORTH | EAST | SOUTH | WEST
physical anchors = dynamic ordered slots per side
```

The current eight-port idea should be treated as the first allocator capacity:

```text
NORTH slot 0 + NORTH overflow slot
EAST  slot 0 + EAST  overflow slot
SOUTH slot 0 + SOUTH overflow slot
WEST  slot 0 + WEST  overflow slot
```

That gives every canonical side one cardinal slot and one neighboring lane. This is enough for many reciprocal-pair cases:

```text
A → D
D → A
```

or:

```text
D → B
B → D
```

The point is to avoid two opposite-direction routes sharing the same diamond vertex or visually collapsing into one line. But the allocator must be able to grow beyond eight when the graph needs it:

```text
slot 0, slot -1, slot +1, slot -2, slot +2, ...
```

Do not expose `N_OVERFLOW`, `E_OVERFLOW`, `S_OVERFLOW`, or `W_OVERFLOW` as durable semantic port names. Overflow is a **physical lane decision**, not the branch meaning. The branch meaning is something like:

```text
primary-input
primary-output
yes
no
feedback
reciprocal
self-loop
container-crossing
fanout-member
fanin-member
```

Recommended internal shape:

```ts
interface PhysicalAnchor {
  semanticPortId: string
  side: PortSide
  slot: number        // 0, -1, +1, -2, +2, ...
  anchorKind:
    | 'diamond-vertex'
    | 'diamond-side-slot'
    | 'shape-boundary-slot'
  x: number
  y: number
}
```

Recommended certificate fragment:

```json
{
  "source": {
    "node": "D",
    "shape": "diamond",
    "side": "WEST",
    "slot": 1,
    "role": "reciprocal",
    "reason": "separate reciprocal pair from opposite-direction edge"
  },
  "target": {
    "node": "A",
    "side": "EAST",
    "slot": -1,
    "role": "reciprocal"
  }
}
```

Blunt policy:

```text
Keep the 8 physical anchors if they are already useful.
Hide them behind a side/slot allocator now.
Never let “diamond has 8 ports” become the public or cross-renderer contract.
```

### Single-edge vertex rule

If exactly one edge uses a diamond side and the lane is clear, attach it to the exact vertex.

Example:

```text
TD yes edge → SOUTH vertex
LR yes edge → EAST vertex
```

### Multi-edge side rule

If multiple edges need the same diamond side, do not stack all of them on the exact vertex. Allocate ordered side slots associated with that side.

Two reasonable approaches:

1. **Vertex-lane plus adjacent offsets**: keep the primary branch on the vertex and place secondary branches near it on adjacent side segments.
2. **Side-slot distribution**: distribute all same-side ports along the relevant diamond boundary interval, preserving order.

The first approach preserves the obvious main branch. The second approach is cleaner for high fanout. Choose by route class:

```text
single primary-forward edge: exact vertex
primary + minor siblings: primary at vertex, siblings offset
large fanout/fanin: ordered side-slot distribution
```

### What not to do for diamonds

Do not:

```text
route to the rectangle bounding box and clip afterward as the source of truth
attach all edges at the diamond center
attach every outgoing branch to whichever side gives the shortest path
let the crossing minimizer swap yes/no without recording a reason
stack multiple branches on one exact vertex
move a no/else branch onto the primary-forward side silently
```

## Other flowchart shapes

The following table gives recommended canonical sites and special rules. “Four canonical sites” usually means `NORTH`, `EAST`, `SOUTH`, and `WEST`, but the exact contact point must be computed from the real shape outline.

| Shape family | Canonical sites | Actual ports | Special rule |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Rectangle / process | 4 sides | dynamic, per edge endpoint or branch group | Use side midpoints for single primary edges; ordered side slots for fanout/fanin. |
| Rounded rectangle | 4 sides | dynamic | Same as rectangle, but exact contact should respect rounded outline if visible. |
| Stadium / terminator | 4 sides | dynamic, but role-restricted | Start-like nodes should warn on unexpected incoming edges; end-like nodes should warn on unexpected outgoing edges unless Mermaid semantics allow them. |
| Diamond / decision | 4 vertices | dynamic | Exact vertex for single clear side edge; ordered side/near-vertex slots for multiple edges. |
| Circle / connector | 4 cardinal sites, optional 8 candidates internally | dynamic | Use ray/ellipse intersection; radial anchors are fine internally, but exported semantic sides should remain stable. |
| Double circle | 4 cardinal sites, optional 8 candidates internally | dynamic | Same as circle; route to outer boundary, not inner ring. |
| Hexagon / prepare | 4 sides plus shape-aware contact | dynamic | Use route ray intersection with polygon, not rectangular clipping. |
| Parallelogram / input-output | 4 sides plus slanted-edge oracle | dynamic | Primary flow should still use graph-direction sides; exact contact must account for slant. |
| Trapezoid / manual operation | 4 sides plus slanted-edge oracle | dynamic | Same principle: semantic side first, polygon contact second. |
| Database / cylinder | 4 side roles, rim-aware contact | dynamic | Avoid top/bottom rim artifacts; primary side should be graph-directional unless syntax/role says otherwise. |
| Subroutine / predefined process | 4 sides | dynamic | Treat boundary as process-like; internal vertical bars are decoration unless the family gives them semantics. |
| Document / multi-document | 4 sides plus document-outline contact | dynamic | Prefer stable side anchors; bottom wave should not randomly absorb normal primary-forward edges. |
| Subgraph / container | boundary sides | one boundary port per crossing edge or crossing group | Cross-hierarchy edges should pass through explicit boundary ports/proxy edges. |
| Small junction / architecture junction | 4 cardinal sites, optional radial candidates | dynamic | High-degree junctions should distribute ports by side and order; avoid unreadable central starbursts. |
| Class / ER entity box | 4 sides, plus family-specific endpoint markers | dynamic | Relation/cardinality markers belong to endpoints; class compartments are not random edge targets. |

## Shape-specific exactness

The side choice is semantic. The contact coordinate is geometric.

That means:

```text
semantic layer: edge exits SOUTH side of diamond
geometry layer: SOUTH side means the rendered diamond's south vertex or an ordered nearby slot
certificate: records both semantic side and exact contact coordinate
```

Do not let the geometry layer override the semantic layer silently. If an edge could not use its intended side, emit a diagnostic.

## Port count policy by node role

### Ordinary process node

Usually:

```text
1 incoming primary port on opposite-flow side
1 outgoing primary port on flow side
```

But actual instances increase with fanout/fanin:

```text
N incoming edges from previous rank -> N ordered input ports
M outgoing edges to next rank       -> M ordered output ports
feedback edge                       -> separate side port
self-loop                           -> self-loop side/corner port
```

### Decision node

Usually:

```text
1 incoming primary
1 primary/yes output
1 alternate/no output
```

But dynamic:

```text
N incoming branches -> ordered incoming ports
M yes/success targets -> ordered primary-output ports or fanout group
K no/failure/else targets -> ordered alternate-side ports
feedback -> non-primary side port
self-loop -> self-loop side/corner port
```

### Start/end nodes

Do not enforce graph-theory purity too hard because Mermaid users sometimes abuse shapes. But diagnostics should exist.

```text
start-like: outgoing expected, incoming suspicious
end-like: incoming expected, outgoing suspicious
```

### Containers/subgraphs

A container should not behave like a normal node. It needs boundary ports.

```text
inside node -> container boundary port -> outside node
outside node -> container boundary port -> inside node
container-id endpoint -> boundary port chosen by route class
```

The boundary port should be visible in layout JSON and certificates even if it is not drawn as a visible dot.

## How to decide port side

Use this order of authority:

1. **Explicit syntax**, if Agentic Mermaid ever introduces or preserves explicit side/port metadata.
2. **Diagram family contract**, e.g. flowchart/state/class/ER/architecture.
3. **Graph direction**, e.g. `TD`, `BT`, `LR`, `RL`.
4. **Route class**, e.g. primary-forward, feedback, fanout, self-loop, container-edge.
5. **Node role and shape**, e.g. decision diamond vs process box vs connector.
6. **Branch label hints**, e.g. yes/no/true/false/success/failure.
7. **Source/model order**, as a soft order constraint.
8. **Crossing/length/router cost**, as a tie-breaker, not as the source of meaning.
9. **Fallback/relaxation**, only with a diagnostic and certificate.

Blunt rule:

> Geometry optimization may choose between valid semantic candidates. It may not silently invent the semantics.

## Direction mapping

Use a primary axis and two side axes.

```text
TD: primary out SOUTH, primary in NORTH, side branches EAST/WEST
BT: primary out NORTH, primary in SOUTH, side branches EAST/WEST
LR: primary out EAST,  primary in WEST,  side branches NORTH/SOUTH
RL: primary out WEST,  primary in EAST,  side branches NORTH/SOUTH
```

Feedback normally uses a non-primary side unless the graph analysis proves the edge is not actually feedback.

## Ordering policy

For each node side:

```text
1. group by route class and semantic role
2. preserve source/model order inside each group
3. keep primary-forward closest to the canonical center/vertex
4. place alternate branches consistently on the chosen alternate side
5. allow crossing minimization to reorder only when the constraint is soft
6. record whether order was preserved, optimized, or relaxed
```

Suggested certificate fields:

```ts
interface PortCertificate {
  edgeId: string
  endpoint: 'source' | 'target'
  nodeId: string
  routeClass: RouteClass
  intendedSide: PortSide
  actualSide: PortSide
  portRole?: string
  portOrder?: number
  exactAnchor: { x: number; y: number }
  shapeContact: 'exact' | 'slot' | 'clipped' | 'relaxed'
  constraint: PortConstraint
  diagnostics: string[]
}
```

## ASCII/Unicode projection

ASCII should not recalculate semantics from scratch.

Pipeline:

```text
semantic edge -> route class -> port side/order -> SVG/layout coordinate -> grid-cell projection
```

The ASCII renderer may need to degrade geometry, but it should not silently change the side or branch ownership.

Diagnostics:

```text
ASCII_PORT_PROJECTION_DEGRADED
ASCII_LABEL_MOVED_FROM_BRANCH
ASCII_ROUTE_COLLAPSED
ASCII_CONTAINER_BOUNDARY_AMBIGUOUS
```

## Acceptance criteria for a port/anchor issue

A focused port issue should include fixtures for:

```text
TD decision diamond: yes down, no side
LR decision diamond: yes right, no vertical side
BT/RL mirrored decision diamonds
fanout from a process node with ordered output ports
fanin into a process node with ordered input ports
feedback edge that avoids the primary-forward lane
self-loop on rectangle, diamond, circle
subgraph/container crossing with boundary port
circle connector with exact outline endpoint
parallelogram/trapezoid/hexagon with polygon contact oracle
cylinder/database with rim-aware contact
SVG/ASCII/Unicode route-intent parity
layout JSON exposes port choices and certificates
constraint relaxation emits structured diagnostics
```

Minimum red-first tests:

```text
wrong side fails
wrong order fails when order is fixed
edge endpoint off shape outline fails
edge endpoint on bounding box instead of real shape fails
silent fallback fails
ASCII side mismatch fails
route certificate missing fails
```

## Recommended issue title

```text
Define semantic port/anchor contract for flowchart/state routing across SVG, ASCII/Unicode, and layout JSON
```

## Recommended issue body

```md
## Problem

Agentic Mermaid currently has route-contract work, but the next durable layer is a stable semantic port/anchor contract. We need one model of edge endpoint intent that SVG, PNG, ASCII/Unicode, and layout JSON all consume.

A shape should not have a fixed hard-coded number of total ports. It should expose canonical anchor sites. The diagram semantics and incident edges should instantiate ordered port instances on those sites.

## Proposal

Define:

- canonical anchor sites per shape family
- dynamic port instances per edge endpoint / branch group
- default side mapping for TD/BT/LR/RL
- decision-diamond yes/no/feedback policy
- reciprocal-pair slot allocation without hard-coding diamond=8 semantic ports
- fanout/fanin ordering policy
- boundary ports for subgraphs/containers
- shape-specific contact oracles
- port certificates in layout JSON
- SVG/ASCII/Unicode parity checks
- diagnostics for side/order/contact relaxation

## Key policy

A diamond has four canonical anchor sites: NORTH, EAST, SOUTH, WEST. It does not have exactly four total ports, and it should not be modeled as exactly eight semantic ports either. Eight physical anchors can be the initial allocator capacity: one cardinal slot plus one overflow slot per side. The durable contract is side + dynamic ordered slot + semantic role + certificate reason.

## Out of scope

- public Mermaid.js syntax changes
- pixel parity with Mermaid.js
- generic typography/accessibility/security rewrites
- every Mermaid family at once
- fixed-position ports everywhere
```

issue.body:
## Codex Desktop version

26.730.61639 (build 6234)

## Subscription

Not included; this is a local rendering issue and does not appear subscription-dependent.

## Platform

macOS — Darwin 25.5.0, Apple Silicon (arm64)

## Description

Mermaid `stateDiagram-v2` blocks can render transition labels on top of one another in Codex Desktop. With reverse transitions, a self-loop, and longer CJK labels, the label `准备失败或取消预占` overlaps a neighboring transition label, making the diagram difficult to read.

This report intentionally excludes account information, local paths, conversation IDs, private repository names, and other workspace content.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open Codex Desktop.
2. Render an assistant Markdown response containing:

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> IDLE

    IDLE --> DISPATCHING: "reserve：抢到执行权"
    DISPATCHING --> RUNNING: "tryStart：启动 Agent，generation + 1"
    RUNNING --> IDLE: "end：正常结束"
    IDLE --> IDLE: "暂无任务"
    DISPATCHING --> IDLE: "准备失败或取消预占"
    RUNNING --> IDLE: "forceEnd：取消或异常恢复"
```

3. Observe the transition labels near the `IDLE` / `DISPATCHING` edge.

## Actual behavior

The long transition label overlaps another edge label. The text becomes partially obscured even though the diagram container has ample horizontal space.

## Expected behavior

Transition labels should be laid out without colliding, or Codex Desktop should use a layout/fallback that keeps all labels legible.

## Additional context

- The desktop bundle's third-party notices identify Mermaid 11.16.0.
- The packaged renderer initializes Mermaid with `htmlLabels: false` and renders the SVG directly; no post-layout collision handling was observed.
- Codex Desktop sanitizes Mermaid init directives, so users cannot reliably apply a per-diagram layout workaround.
- A related upstream Mermaid state-diagram layout issue is https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/issues/6336, though this report specifically concerns overlapping transition labels in the Codex Desktop rendering surface.

data.title: fix(dagre): merge flowchart and state self-loop segments before rendering
data.body: ## :bookmark_tabs: Summary Fixes flowchart and stateDiagram-v2 self-loop edges so that one logical self-loop is rendered as one SVG `` instead of three internal dagre layout segments. Resolves #6336 ### Background I first noticed this while frequently editing Mermaid flowcharts through the GUI at https://mermaid.ai/. That editor is not part of this open-source repository, but it made the issue very visible: self-loop edges could not be edited reliably through the GUI. Deleting the edge, selecting it, or editing its text did not work the same way as regular edges. After inspecting the generated SVG, I found that a single logical self-loop such as: ```mermaid flowchart TD C --> C ``` was not represented as a single SVG edge path. Instead, it was rendered as multiple `` elements with internal ids similar to: ```html ``` This made downstream SVG-based tooling treat one logical edge as several visual edges. The same multi-path self-loop behavior was also visible when testing in Mermaid's own rendering output, so the root issue appeared to be in Mermaid core rendering rather than only in external GUI tooling. This PR changes the final SVG output for flowcharts and stateDiagram-v2 diagrams so that a logical self-loop edge maps back to a single rendered path. ### Before / After Before: clicking a self-loop edge selects one of three split SVG path segments instead of a single logical edge, so GUI operations such as editing the label or deleting the edge do not work reliably. After: the same self-loop now appears as one compact SVG path for the logical edge, preventing the GUI from treating its internal layout segments as separate editable edges. ## :straight_ruler: Design Decisions ### Root Cause The issue comes from the dagre layout adapter: ```text packages/mermaid/src/rendering-util/layout-algorithms/dagre/index.js ``` For self-loops, the adapter intentionally creates dummy nodes and splits one logical edge into three internal layout edges: ```text node -> dummy node 1 -> dummy node 2 -> node ``` That workaround is useful for layout because it gives dagre a route that can produce a loop-like shape. The problem was that these internal layout segments were still passed directly to the SVG edge renderer after layout. Since the renderer draws one `` per edge object, one logical self-loop became three public SVG paths. ### Chosen Fix This PR keeps the existing dagre dummy-node workaround for layout stability, but converts flowchart and stateDiagram-v2 self-loop segments back into one render edge before SVG insertion. The new flow is: ```text Input: C --> C Dagre layout graph: C -> dummy1 -> dummy2 -> C Render preparation: group the three self-loop segments by the original edge id compute one compact self-loop route around the node create one merged render edge Final SVG: one logical self-loop = one ``` This avoids relying on dagre to natively produce good self-loop geometry for every rank direction, node shape, label size, and cluster case. At the same time, it prevents internal layout implementation details from leaking into the final SVG DOM. ### Why Not Remove the Dummy Edges Entirely? The simplest-looking change would be to stop splitting self-loops and call dagre with a direct self-edge: ```js graph.setEdge(nodeId, nodeId, edge, edge.id); ``` I did not choose that approach because the existing dummy-node logic appears to be there to stabilize self-loop layout. Removing it would change the layout input more dramatically and could introduce regressions in complex diagrams. Instead, this PR makes a smaller change: - keep the layout workaround - preserve the original edge metadata on the three internal segments - merge those segments immediately before rendering - render one path for the logical self-loop - leave class diagrams on the existing segmented rendering path because self-referential multiplicity labels rely on that behavior ### Compact Self-loop Shape Simply concatenating dagre's three segment point lists can still produce very large or awkward self-loops. This PR computes a compact loop around the original node for the final render edge. The generated loop uses: - the original node position - the original node width and height - the self-loop label size - the graph direction - dagre's dummy node positions as layout hints This keeps the self-loop visually small and close to the node, instead of producing a long route that looks like several unrelated edge segments. ### Side Selection The self-loop is not always forced to the top of the node. The implementation first looks at where dagre placed the dummy nodes and uses that as a hint for which side of the node the loop should attach to. If those hints are unavailable, it falls back to the graph direction: ```text TB -> top BT -> bottom LR -> right RL -> left ``` This keeps the loop placement closer to dagre's layout result while still producing deterministic output. ### Label Handling Before layout, edge labels are inserted while the three self-loop layout segments already exist. To avoid duplicate labels, only the middle segment inserts the label. During that label insertion, the segment temporarily uses the original edge id so that the label is associated with the final merged render edge. This merged-path behavior is scoped to `flowchart`, `flowchart-v2`, and `stateDiagram`. Other dagre-based diagrams, including class diagrams, keep the previous segmented self-loop rendering behavior. ### Fallback Behavior If a self-loop group does not contain exactly three expected segments, the implementation falls back to rendering the original segments rather than dropping the edge. This is intentional. In unexpected graph states, preserving the previous visible output is safer than making the edge disappear. ### Files Changed ```text packages/mermaid/src/rendering-util/layout-algorithms/dagre/index.js packages/mermaid/src/rendering-util/layout-algorithms/dagre/index.spec.js cypress/integration/rendering/flowchart/flowchart-v2.spec.js cypress/integration/rendering/state/stateDiagram-v2.spec.js ``` ### Tests Added Added targeted tests for the dagre self-loop rendering flow: - verifies that three internal self-loop layout segments become one render edge - verifies that self-loop side placement can follow dagre layout hints - verifies that regular edges pass through unchanged - renders a real Mermaid flowchart in JSDOM and checks that the self-loop appears as one SVG path - verifies that internal `cyclic-special` path ids are not exposed as rendered self-loop paths - verifies that the generated self-loop route stays compact - adds Cypress visual coverage for labeled flowchart self-loops - adds Cypress visual coverage for non-TB flowchart self-loop directions - adds Cypress visual coverage for the #6336 `stateDiagram-v2` self-loop reproduction Targeted command run: ```sh pnpm exec vitest run packages/mermaid/src/rendering-util/layout-algorithms/dagre/index.spec.js ``` Result: ```text 1 test file passed 5 tests passed ``` The test run also emitted existing Vite/TypeScript `TS5055: Cannot write file ... because it would overwrite input file` warnings, but those warnings did not fail the targeted test suite. ### Expected Impact After this change: - a logical self-loop edge renders as one SVG path - self-loop internals such as `cyclic-special-1`, `cyclic-special-mid`, and `cyclic-special-2` are no longer exposed as separate rendered paths - SVG-based tools can map a self-loop path back to a single logical edge more reliably - Updated the patch to scope self-loop segment merging to flowcharts only.

The failing E2E case was a class diagram self-reference with multiplicity labels. Class diagrams also use the dagre self-loop segment workaround, but they rely on the existing segmented rendering for terminal label placement. To avoid changing non-flowchart behavior, self-loop merging is now enabled only for `flowchart` / `flowchart-v2`, and I added a unit test to ensure segments are preserved when merging is disabled.

[sisyphus-bot]

Thanks for the careful work here, and especially for the outstanding PR description — the root-cause walkthrough, the "why not remove dummy edges" explanation, and the before/after screenshots make this PR very easy to review. Really appreciate the contribution.

## What's working well

- 🎉 **[praise]** The chosen approach is exactly the kind of minimal-risk fix this codebase rewards: keep the dagre dummy-node workaround so layout stability isn't disturbed, and collapse the three internal segments into one render edge right at the SVG boundary. Scope is well-controlled and the gating to `flowchart` / `flowchart-v2` keeps state/class/etc. on the existing path.
- 🎉 **[praise]** Excellent fallback behavior — if a self-loop group doesn't have exactly three segments, the code falls back to rendering the original segments instead of dropping the edge (`index.js:191-193`). This is the right default for an unexpected graph state.
- 🎉 **[praise]** Side selection from dagre's dummy-node placement (`getSelfLoopSide`) instead of always forcing top is a nice touch — keeps the visual closer to the layout engine's intent while still being deterministic.
- 🎉 **[praise]** Bonus: the diff incidentally fixes a latent typo in the third self-loop segment id — `nodeId + '-cyc<lic-special-2'` (introduced way back in `3b3b599c3`) becomes `'-cyclic-special-2'`. Nice catch.

## Things to address

- 🟡 **[important]** **Linked-issue scope mismatch.** The PR description says `Resolves #6336`, but #6336's reproduction is `stateDiagram-v2 ... Node --> Node: Self Edge` and the title is "Self-edges/loops look very awkward in **state** diagrams." The new gating in `index.js`:
  ```js
  const shouldMergeSelfLoopSegments = (diagramType) =>
    diagramType === 'flowchart' || diagramType === 'flowchart-v2';
  ```
  excludes state diagrams (`stateDetector.ts:7` registers `id = 'state'`), so #6336's actual reproduction case will keep rendering as before. Two reasonable paths forward — happy with either:
  1. Widen the gating to state (and possibly class) diagrams, with at least one Cypress imgSnapshotTest per included diagram type to verify the new geometry looks right.
  2. Reframe the PR as "fix(flowchart): merge self-loop layout segments before rendering" and change `Resolves #6336` to `Refs #6336` (or `Helps with #6336`), leaving the issue open for state-diagram follow-up.
- 🟡 **[important]** **Locking in the new self-loop geometry visually.** Existing Cypress coverage at `cypress/integration/rendering/flowchart/flowchart-v2.spec.js:1098` exercises self-loops in nested clusters in `TB` direction without labels — Argos will catch any visual regression there, which is great. But the new code introduces meaningful behavior that's not yet under visual test:
  - **Labeled self-loops** — `getSelfLoopLabelPosition` and the label-segment temporary id swap in `recursiveRender` are unique to this PR; an `A -- "label text" --> A` case would lock that in.
  - **`LR` / `RL` / `BT` side selection** — `getSelfLoopSide` and `getSelfLoopPoints` return four different shapes per direction; right now only the `TB` default branch is covered.
  - **Hint-driven side selection** — when dagre's dummy-node positions push the loop to a non-default side, the second unit test at `index.spec.js:117` covers the math, but a Cypress case would lock in the visual outcome.

  Adding a couple of new `imgSnapshotTest()` cases in `flowchart-v2.spec.js` would meaningfully reduce the regression risk on the new geometry.

## Suggestions

- 💡 **[suggestion]** Could you confirm `pnpm e2e` was run end-to-end? Per `CLAUDE.md`: *"`rendering-util/` is shared by all diagram types. Changes here can regress any diagram. Always run full e2e tests (`pnpm e2e`) after modifying shared rendering code"*. The merge logic itself is gated to flowchart, but the typo fix on the third-segment id (`cyc<lic-special-2` → `cyclic-special-2`) and the small refactor of the edge-iteration loop in `recursiveRender` apply to all dagre consumers, so it's worth confirming nothing regressed in state/class.

- 🟢 **[nit]** `setOnProtectedConstant(object, key, value)` in `index.spec.js:8` is just `object[key] = value` — the wrapper name implies real protection logic that isn't there. A direct assignment (or just `vi.stubGlobal` / `vi.spyOn`) would be clearer, and the test setup has a few Vitest-friendly idioms it could lean on.

## :bookmark_tabs: Summary Fixes flowchart and stateDiagram-v2 self-loop edges so that one logical self-loop is rendered as one SVG `` instead of three internal dagre layout segments. Resolves #6336 ### Background I first noticed this while frequently editing Mermaid flowcharts through the GUI at https://mermaid.ai/. That editor is not part of this open-source repository, but it made the issue very visible: self-loop edges could not be edited reliably through the GUI. Deleting the edge, selecting it, or editing its text did not work the same way as regular edges. After inspecting the generated SVG, I found that a single logical self-loop such as: ```mermaid flowchart TD C --> C ``` was not represented as a single SVG edge path. Instead, it was rendered as multiple `` elements with internal ids similar to: ```html ``` This made downstream SVG-based tooling treat one logical edge as several visual edges. The same multi-path self-loop behavior was also visible when testing in Mermaid's own rendering output, so the root issue appeared to be in Mermaid core rendering rather than only in external GUI tooling. This PR changes the final SVG output for flowcharts and stateDiagram-v2 diagrams so that a logical self-loop edge maps back to a single rendered path. ### Before / After Before: clicking a self-loop edge selects one of three split SVG path segments instead of a single logical edge, so GUI operations such as editing the label or deleting the edge do not work reliably. After: the same self-loop now appears as one compact SVG path for the logical edge, preventing the GUI from treating its internal layout segments as separate editable edges. ## :straight_ruler: Design Decisions ### Root Cause The issue comes from the dagre layout adapter: ```text packages/mermaid/src/rendering-util/layout-algorithms/dagre/index.js ``` For self-loops, the adapter intentionally creates dummy nodes and splits one logical edge into three internal layout edges: ```text node -> dummy node 1 -> dummy node 2 -> node ``` That workaround is useful for layout because it gives dagre a route that can produce a loop-like shape. The problem was that these internal layout segments were still passed directly to the SVG edge renderer after layout. Since the renderer draws one `` per edge object, one logical self-loop became three public SVG paths. ### Chosen Fix This PR keeps the existing dagre dummy-node workaround for layout stability, but converts flowchart and stateDiagram-v2 self-loop segments back into one render edge before SVG insertion. The new flow is: ```text Input: C --> C Dagre layout graph: C -> dummy1 -> dummy2 -> C Render preparation: group the three self-loop segments by the original edge id compute one compact self-loop route around the node create one merged render edge Final SVG: one logical self-loop = one ``` This avoids relying on dagre to natively produce good self-loop geometry for every rank direction, node shape, label size, and cluster case. At the same time, it prevents internal layout implementation details from leaking into the final SVG DOM. ### Why Not Remove the Dummy Edges Entirely? The simplest-looking change would be to stop splitting self-loops and call dagre with a direct self-edge: ```js graph.setEdge(nodeId, nodeId, edge, edge.id); ``` I did not choose that approach because the existing dummy-node logic appears to be there to stabilize self-loop layout. Removing it would change the layout input more dramatically and could introduce regressions in complex diagrams. Instead, this PR makes a smaller change: - keep the layout workaround - preserve the original edge metadata on the three internal segments - merge those segments immediately before rendering - render one path for the logical self-loop - leave class diagrams on the existing segmented rendering path because self-referential multiplicity labels rely on that behavior ### Compact Self-loop Shape Simply concatenating dagre's three segment point lists can still produce very large or awkward self-loops. This PR computes a compact loop around the original node for the final render edge. The generated loop uses: - the original node position - the original node width and height - the self-loop label size - the graph direction - dagre's dummy node positions as layout hints This keeps the self-loop visually small and close to the node, instead of producing a long route that looks like several unrelated edge segments. ### Side Selection The self-loop is not always forced to the top of the node. The implementation first looks at where dagre placed the dummy nodes and uses that as a hint for which side of the node the loop should attach to. If those hints are unavailable, it falls back to the graph direction: ```text TB -> top BT -> bottom LR -> right RL -> left ``` This keeps the loop placement closer to dagre's layout result while still producing deterministic output. ### Label Handling Before layout, edge labels are inserted while the three self-loop layout segments already exist. To avoid duplicate labels, only the middle segment inserts the label. During that label insertion, the segment temporarily uses the original edge id so that the label is associated with the final merged render edge. This merged-path behavior is scoped to `flowchart`, `flowchart-v2`, and `stateDiagram`. Other dagre-based diagrams, including class diagrams, keep the previous segmented self-loop rendering behavior. ### Fallback Behavior If a self-loop group does not contain exactly three expected segments, the implementation falls back to rendering the original segments rather than dropping the edge. This is intentional. In unexpected graph states, preserving the previous visible output is safer than making the edge disappear. ### Files Changed ```text packages/mermaid/src/rendering-util/layout-algorithms/dagre/index.js packages/mermaid/src/rendering-util/layout-algorithms/dagre/index.spec.js cypress/integration/rendering/flowchart/flowchart-v2.spec.js cypress/integration/rendering/state/stateDiagram-v2.spec.js ``` ### Tests Added Added targeted tests for the dagre self-loop rendering flow: - verifies that three internal self-loop layout segments become one render edge - verifies that self-loop side placement can follow dagre layout hints - verifies that regular edges pass through unchanged - renders a real Mermaid flowchart in JSDOM and checks that the self-loop appears as one SVG path - verifies that internal `cyclic-special` path ids are not exposed as rendered self-loop paths - verifies that the generated self-loop route stays compact - adds Cypress visual coverage for labeled flowchart self-loops - adds Cypress visual coverage for non-TB flowchart self-loop directions - adds Cypress visual coverage for the #6336 `stateDiagram-v2` self-loop reproduction Targeted command run: ```sh pnpm exec vitest run packages/mermaid/src/rendering-util/layout-algorithms/dagre/index.spec.js ``` Result: ```text 1 test file passed 5 tests passed ``` The test run also emitted existing Vite/TypeScript `TS5055: Cannot write file ... because it would overwrite input file` warnings, but those warnings did not fail the targeted test suite. ### Expected Impact After this change: - a logical self-loop edge renders as one SVG path - self-loop internals such as `cyclic-special-1`, `cyclic-special-mid`, and `cyclic-special-2` are no longer exposed as separate rendered paths - SVG-based tools can map a self-loop path back to a single logical edge more reliably - self-loop geometry is more compact and visually attached to the node - regular edges keep their existing rendering behavior - stateDiagram-v2 self-loops use the same compact single-path rendering - class diagrams keep their existing segmented self-loop behavior This should also help SVG-based GUI editors, including Mermaid AI, map flowchart self-loops back to a single editable edge for selection, deletion, and label editing. ### :clipboard: Tasks Make sure you -
